mechanistic_interpretation.supported: The current checkpoint path permits up to 96 GB of in-flight serialization bytes per PyTree handler while the composite checkpoint contains two large PyTree items, train_state and params. This source-level concurrency budget is grossly mismatched to the 40/64 GiB cgroup ceilings and is a direct engineering target for bounded staging.
mechanistic_interpretation.not_claimed: The source audit alone does not prove exact per-item simultaneous peak residency or guarantee a 4 GB limiter will pass; that requires the prospective qualification below.

prospective_repair.name: THROTTLED_SYNCHRONOUS_CHECKPOINT_4GB_PER_PYTREE_ITEM
prospective_repair.selection_rationale: 4 GB/item is a single conservative source-native limiter chosen before execution. With two large PyTree items this caps their serialization in-flight allowances far below the 40 GiB cgroup instead of allowing 96 GB/item. No limiter ladder is authorized.
prospective_repair.if_pass: Stop resource qualification and design a separate fresh run3 authority using the same 4 GB/item synchronous checkpoint implementation plus completion barrier.
prospective_repair.if_fail: STOP checkpoint resource repair. Do not test another limiter, higher MemoryMax, altered checkpoint content/format/frequency, or formal run3 without a new independently reviewed design.
